source.title: Insert or Divert: A Trigger-free Removability Criterion for LLM Backdoors
source.citation: Insert or Divert: A Trigger-free Remo…

page_placements.theme: Backdoor behaviours mediated by single residual directions that overlap the refusal subspace

record.tranche_reason: It causally resets a residual-stream difference direction and measures changes in a compliance-versus-refusal next-token score, but the direction is triggered-minus-clean for backdoors, not the claim’s harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction; the intervention is also limited to selected layers and the final prompt token.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports layer scans used to choose intervention layers; those values are not included as rows because they are used for layer selection. Its Triage ASR results combine ablation with recovery training, so they do not isolate the ablation effect. The main direct intervention results are the score-gap reductions in Table 6.
record.test_reason: The study works in a new setting: LoRA data-poisoning backdoors on Llama-2-7B-chat. Finding 2 measures how the trigger-induced shift aligns with the native harmful-minus-benign refusal axis (Arditi et al.). Jailbreak-backdoor drift points against that axis (−0.68) and targeted-refusal drift points along it (+0.70). This bears on whether attacks act by suppressing the refusal direction (V3). The causal resets in Table 6 use a triggered-minus-clean backdoor direction, not the claim's direction, so they fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors find jailbreak backdoors insert a shared late-layer direction opposing the native refusal axis (cosine −0.68). Targeted-refusal backdoors instead recruit the native refusal representation (+0.70), so they need attenuation rather than ablation. TRIAGE cuts mean jailbreak ASR to 0.2% and targeted-refusal ASR to 0.6%. The costs are a perplexity rise (7.8 to about 13) and weaker repair under adaptive attack.
record.recipe_differences: The study resets a triggered-minus-clean residual difference to a clean projection, but tests backdoored Llama chat models rather than the original harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. The reset is applied at selected blocks and the final prompt token, not every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The intervention layer matters: the paper reports layer-dependent causal effects and selects layers using surrogate attacks. The reported single-block score-gap reductions also differ across trigger formats.

fits_no_version.finding: At the best single block, resetting a triggered-minus-clean backdoor direction to its mean clean projection closes 68–89% of the gap in a compliance-vs-refusal next-token score (BadNet, VPI, CTBA on Llama-2-7B-chat). Closure reaches 87–97% with 12 blocks (unverified).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single residual direction inserted by a jailbreak backdoor causally mediates most of the backdoor's anti-refusal effect.

fits_no_version.finding: An adaptive BadNet adapter trained to stay orthogonal to a reference backdoor direction (cosine 0.786 to 0.003) keeps 95.9% triggered ASR. After oracle ablation plus recovery its ASR is 21.2%, versus 2.0% for the control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Backdoor jailbreak behaviour does not require alignment with a fixed backdoor direction.

record.peer_reviewed: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027
record.problems: The direct causal diagnostic uses a small set of eight matched pairs per adapter and measures next-token probability on fixed opening-token sets, not generated refusal behavior. Its interventions are descriptive rather than held-out defense evaluations. Table 6’s single-block figures are reconstructed from saved diagnostic scores; the paper states that original multi-block patching outputs are unavailable and the K>1 entries remain unverified. The utility evaluation reports a WikiText-2 perplexity increase and does not measure retention of adapter-specific benign capabilities.
record.rows_left_out: Table 6 results for K>1 were left out because they test multiple block resets rather than the single-direction condition and the paper says those original multi-block outputs remain unverified. Layerwise scans and Figure 2a effects used to select intervention layers were also left out under the rule excluding values used only for layer selection.

untested.parts: The native harmful-minus-harmless direction is never ablated or added. Only backdoor-direction resets are done.

Not tested: prompt-based jailbreaks (only poisoned-adapter backdoors are studied), causal evidence that suppressing the refusal direction produces compliance, and training against refusal-direction ablation for robustness. Alignment is reported for BadNet only.
No abliteration or weight edit of the refusal direction.
No comparison of multi-direction or cone accounts.
Harm judgment and refusal are not separated.
No test of refusal-direction transfer across languages or model variants.

missing.what: Signed cosine between backdoor drift and the native harmful-minus-benign refusal axis: jailbreak −0.68, targeted refusal +0.70, negative sentiment +0.22 (BadNet).
AUC of a native refusal probe trained without triggers: 0.00 on jailbreak activations, 1.00/0.99 on targeted-refusal activations (BadNet/VPI), 0.73 on negative sentiment.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 link is wrong. Its rows reset a backdoor triggered-minus-clean direction, not the claim's direction. The only link to the claim's direction is the alignment analysis with the Arditi refusal axis, which no row records. The Table 6 K=1 values are in-sample best-block maxima on 8 pairs. Defense ASR results combine ablation of the backdoor direction with fine-tuning and do not test any version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce refusals, ablation at every layer and position, the original harmful-minus-harmless direction, or broad retention of general abilities as a consequence of the isolated ablation.
No weight-edit implementation of ablation is evaluated.

The adaptive experiment trains a backdoor to reduce alignment with a reference direction; it does not test whether jailbreak attacks suppress the claimed refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
The study does not compare affine, cone, or multiple-refusal-direction accounts.
It does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
Its repair transfer across backbones does not test transfer of the claimed refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
It does not vary safety-training procedures or timing to test their effect on the existence of a removable refusal direction.

relationships.reason: Based on the text (Finding 2, Appendix A.1), not on rows. Jailbreak drift has cosine −0.68 with the native refusal axis, and a native-refusal probe scores AUC 0.00 on jailbreak activations. This is consistent with the backdoor suppressing refusal. The evidence is correlational only.
relationships.display_finding: Jailbreak drift had cosine similarity −0.68 with the native refusal axis, and a native-refusal probe scored AUC 0.00 on jailbreak activations, providing correlational evidence of suppression.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: BadNet jailbreak backdoor LoRA on Llama-2-7B-chat, late layers
labels.reason: Text (Section 3.1 Finding 2, Appendix A.1): BadNet jailbreak drift has signed cosine -0.68 with the harmful-minus-benign axis, and a trigger-naive refusal probe gives AUC 0.00 on jailbreak activations. The authors call this a 'shared anti-refusal direction'. The evidence is correlational on one model. The 'training against ablation adds robustness' half of V3 is untested, because TRIAGE ablates a backdoor direction, not the refusal direction.

relation.reason: The study measures how trigger-induced shifts align with the native refusal axis, and reports that jailbreak backdoors oppose it. That result bears directly on whether attacks work by suppressing the direction.

tranche.reason: The setting is new (LoRA data-poisoning backdoors on Llama-2-7B-chat), and it has a result on V3: the jailbreak drift's signed cosine with the Arditi harmful-minus-benign axis is -0.68, with probe AUC 0.00. The study's own question is backdoor removal, not the refusal direction, so T2 (the reader's first call) fits less well.

source_check.notes: The pack's single verdict line has no [lN] id, so label_id is left empty. The text is internally inconsistent: Section 3.1 says the reset effect is strongest after block 15, while Appendix D says mean profiles peak at block 30, and the Table 6 best blocks come from a separate 6-25 scan. The ICLR reviewer-guideline footer is venue boilerplate for human reviewers, not an instruction to an AI reader.

statements.problem: None for this study. The BadNet drift cosine -0.68, targeted-refusal +0.70, jailbreak probe AUC 0.00 and targeted-refusal AUC 1.00/0.99 (BadNet/VPI) all match Section 3.1 Finding 2 and Appendix A.1. Note the signed cosine points against the axis, not just off it.

statements.correction: Jailbreak drift cosine -0.68 is stated for BadNet (Section 3.1). The jailbreak probe AUC 0.00 is given without a per-trigger split. VPI appears only as targeted-refusal probe AUC 0.99. Late-layer residual stream, Llama-2-7B-chat. No projection magnitude is measured.
statements.problem: differences_stated attaches 'BadNet/VPI LoRA adapters' to this study's jailbreak evidence. VPI appears only in the targeted-refusal probe AUC, not in the jailbreak results cited.

statements.correction: Resetting the triggered-minus-clean direction at one block closes 68-89% of a next-token compliance-vs-refusal score gap (Table 6; in-sample, 8 pairs). Ablating a surrogate-derived jailbreak direction plus recovery fine-tuning cuts mean jailbreak ASR to 0.2% (n=99). Neither intervention targets the harmful-minus-benign axis; the refusal-axis evidence is signed cosine (-0.68) and probe AUC (0.00) only. An adaptive BadNet adapter keeps 95.92% ASR at cosine 0.003 to a reference BadNet drift direction (Table 3). Its refusal-axis alignment is not reported.
statements.problem: Correct that the study never ablates or restores the native refusal axis. But for this study the backdoor evidence is not 'measurement only': it runs causal interventions on the backdoor direction.

statements.correction: K=1: BadNet 71% (block 22), VPI 89% (block 25), CTBA 68% (block 25). Direction fit and evaluated on the same 8 pairs, scan of blocks 6-25. K=12: BadNet 97, VPI 97, CTBA 87 (Sleeper 94). These are score reductions, not ASR reductions.
statements.problem: Numbers are right. It omits the authors' caveats: K=1 values are reconstructed from saved scores, and K>1 entries are unverified because the original outputs are unavailable.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Single-block residual resets for BadNet, VPI, and CTBA backdoors on Llama-2-7B-chat
reader_labels.reason: The intervention closes 68–89% of the measured score gap, which is substantial but incomplete, and the outcome is a next-token proxy rather than observed refusal behavior (table6-badnet-k1, table6-vpi-k1, table6-ctba-k1).
